title: CHAT APP (WHATSAPP)
subtitle: Chat looks like CRUD until you notice the two users are on different servers and one of them is offline.
footer: DDIA: Ch 5 consistent prefix · Ch 11 at-least-once + idempotency   ·   Similar: Ride sharing · Live comments · Collaborative editor · Stock trading

items: Keep a persistent WebSocket per device; route messages between chat servers with a registry and per-user pub/sub.
Persist each message and add it to the recipient's inbox before acknowledging the sender, so nothing is lost.
Partition by conversation and number messages within it so every device shows the same order.
1:1 and group chats (up to ~100 members)
Send and receive messages in real time
Offline users get messages when they reconnect
Delivery and read receipts; media
Delivery < 500ms when online
Messages never lost
Ordered within a chat
1B DAU
50B messages/day ≈ ~600k msgs/s.
Hundreds of millions of concurrent connections, at ~1M connections per tuned server → hundreds of chat servers.

items: Alice and Bob are usually connected to different servers, so you need routing between them.
A registry (user → server) and a pub/sub channel per user: server 1 publishes to Bob's channel; server 2, which holds Bob's connection, delivers.
Durability first: persist to the messages table and the recipient's inbox before acknowledging Alice.
Never lose a message?
Persist before ack; at-least-once delivery from the inbox; client dedupes by msg_id.
Ordering?
Per-chat sequence numbers, with chat_id as the partition key so one writer orders them (DDIA Ch 5 consistent prefix).
Groups?
Fan-out per member at send time (≤ ~100 members) into inboxes and channels.
Media?
Upload to S3 via presigned URL; the message carries only the object key.
Assuming both users share a server or are always online.
Adding parts before a number shows they are needed.
Ignoring retries, timeouts and crashes.
